thread: Follow the swarm from surveying the land to drawing it on a map, then set out along a marked trail. Measuring instruments become creatures, maps unfold into landscapes, and trail blazes lead the way through real places.

candidates.name: Science Museum Group Collection
candidates.why: Surveying chains, theodolites, levels and stereoscopes offer jointed, sighting, measuring creatures, with individual collection records to explore.

candidates.name: David Rumsey Map Collection
candidates.why: Historical atlases, globes, pictorial maps and unusual projections can unfold into patterned bodies, imagined terrain and networks of routes.

candidates.name: North Country Trail Association
candidates.why: A long marked trail crosses eight states; its route, blue blazes, bridges, trail-building skills and varied landscapes give the map a journey to follow.

candidates.name: USGS National Geospatial Program
candidates.why: Topographic maps, elevation data, waterways and geographic names turn contours, ridges and branching streams into a vocabulary of terrain.

candidates.name: UNSW Surveying and Geospatial Engineering
candidates.why: The virtual instrument museum describes theodolites, leveling instruments and electronic distance meters, including a bridge-setting instrument and an early Geodimeter.

candidates.name: Ice Age Trail Alliance
candidates.why: Wisconsin trail segments pass glacial landforms, while yellow blazes and the work of making and maintaining a path offer creatures a route across the landscape.

candidates.name: Appalachian Trail Conservancy
candidates.why: White blazes, shelters, trail corridors and the communities that care for a long footpath give the swarm a ground-level way to travel.

candidates.name: Royal Geographical Society
candidates.why: Map collections, fieldwork resources and geographical expeditions offer more ways to measure, represent and explore a landscape.
